bundle_f_deltas.DE_compounder_finding_2030_to_2035_swap: REFUTED at 2035 horizon under spec mapping. 2030 NZAV proxy gave DE green-jobs −22.976k (utilities-only mapping: Electricity + Water + Sewerage&waste). 2035 Cedefop spec mapping gives DE green-jobs +347.4k (largest absolute creator in EU): driven primarily by Architectural & engineering +261k, Electricity +85k, R&D +84k, Electrical equipment +27k. Counter-pressure from Sewerage&waste −87k and Gas/steam/AC −24k. CAVEAT: spec mapping treats all R&D and all Architectural & engineering as green-relevant; true climate-attributable share is lower. The 2030 NZAV finding remains valid as a narrow utilities-only reading; the 2035 spec finding is the broader professional-services-inclusive reading. Both belong on the page; the 'DE compounder' framing as a green-jobs contraction story does not survive the broader mapping at 2035 horizon.
bundle_f_deltas.ES_sanity_check_2030_to_2035: Prior 2030 NZAV proxy: ES green-jobs +49k (utilities-only). 2035 Cedefop spec: ES green-jobs +219.1k. Same expansion driver as DE (Architectural & engineering +84k, Sewerage&waste +42k, Water +30k, Electrical equipment +26k, R&D +24k, Electricity +13k). Plus carbon side ES −371k (largest in EU after IT and PL/RO/TR), driven primarily by Agriculture decline + manufacturing displacement.

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=23,965, 2035=35,848, Δ=+11,883; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=3,466, 2035=2,665, Δ=-801; [36] Water supply 2022=2,550, 2035=2,630, Δ=+80; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=23,100, 2035=22,529, Δ=-571; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=71,210, 2035=97,692, Δ=+26,482; [72] Research & Development 2022=21,350, 2035=36,138, Δ=+14,788; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=45,760, 2035=46,705, Δ=+945. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (25% for AT), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.55) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens4_geopolitical_narrative.value: MSC 2025: "Austria, where the far-right Freedom Party was tasked with forming a government for the first time in January, could soon join this group."
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.derivation_method: Direct read of MSC PDFs (Phil-supplied 2026-04-29). MSC frames: 2024 'Lose-Lose?' (relative-gains thinking, Zeitenwende), 2025 'Multipolarization', 2026 'Under Destruction' (wrecking-ball politics, Pax Americana under destruction). Per-country sentence selection: top-scored sentence (50-600 chars, contains country name, ranked by strategic-keyword density) from each available MSC report. Reported in chronological order, most-recent first. Verbatim text in quotes.
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.uncertainty_band: Verbatim citation; uncertainty is in selection (which sentence best represents country framing). Sentence-level selection may miss broader context across the chapter; full-chapter read would refine.

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $16.34B + RU $0.39B / total imports $219.10B = 7.63%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.55) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = CE [0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = S [0.85, 0.85, 0.65, 0.9, 0.85, 0.65].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.note: Acute water scarcity (lowest renewable freshwater per capita in EU) — drought H-confidence

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=248,354, 2035=333,498, Δ=+85,144; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=27,646, 2035=4,058, Δ=-23,588; [36] Water supply 2022=33,783, 2035=33,958, Δ=+175; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=268,217, 2035=181,325, Δ=-86,892; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=824,048, 2035=1,085,350, Δ=+261,302; [72] Research & Development 2022=248,846, 2035=333,040, Δ=+84,194; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=487,563, 2035=514,602, Δ=+27,039. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative: https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/files/skills_forecast_-_germany_2025.pdf

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (89% for DE), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.85) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens4_geopolitical_narrative.value: MSC 2026: "To help bring about the urgently needed rearmament of the continent, Germany can no longer dodge difficult dilemmas involved in supporting Ukraine, driving defense industrial cooperation, and helping others to meet their defense spending commitments." | MSC 2025: "The war in Ukraine alsonominal: exposed the 47bnWest’s depleted stocks of key weapons adjusted: 96bn 57 Japan between Germany and Poland nominal: 52bn adjusted: 68bn M U N I C H S ECU R I T Y R E P O RT 2 0 2 5 systems and the atrophied state of the US defense industrial base."
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.derivation_method: Direct read of MSC PDFs (Phil-supplied 2026-04-29). MSC frames: 2024 'Lose-Lose?' (relative-gains thinking, Zeitenwende), 2025 'Multipolarization', 2026 'Under Destruction' (wrecking-ball politics, Pax Americana under destruction). Per-country sentence selection: top-scored sentence (50-600 chars, contains country name, ranked by strategic-keyword density) from each available MSC report. Reported in chronological order, most-recent first. Verbatim text in quotes.
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.uncertainty_band: Verbatim citation; uncertainty is in selection (which sentence best represents country framing). Sentence-level selection may miss broader context across the chapter; full-chapter read would refine.

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $175.60B + RU $4.24B / total imports $1486.75B = 12.10%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.95) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = W [0.4, 0.45, 0.65, 0.45, 0.45, 0.6].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.note: 2021 Ahrtal/RW Germany floods (joint DE+BE €44B/200+ deaths) — flood-risk assignment H-confidence; drought 2018+2022 affected Rhine shipping

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (154% for DK), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.5) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens4_geopolitical_narrative.value: MSC 2026: "It deprioritizes Europe in favor of the “Western Hemisphere” Mette Frederiksen, Danish and – albeit to a lesser extent – the Indo-Pacific.25 While reiterating that Prime Minister, TV 2, Europe should “take primary responsibility for its own defense, without January 5, 2026 being dominated by any adversarial power,” the document conspicuously refrains from designating Russia as a threat."
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.derivation_method: Direct read of MSC PDFs (Phil-supplied 2026-04-29). MSC frames: 2024 'Lose-Lose?' (relative-gains thinking, Zeitenwende), 2025 'Multipolarization', 2026 'Under Destruction' (wrecking-ball politics, Pax Americana under destruction). Per-country sentence selection: top-scored sentence (50-600 chars, contains country name, ranked by strategic-keyword density) from each available MSC report. Reported in chronological order, most-recent first. Verbatim text in quotes.
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.uncertainty_band: Verbatim citation; uncertainty is in selection (which sentence best represents country framing). Sentence-level selection may miss broader context across the chapter; full-chapter read would refine.

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $7.87B + RU $0.35B / total imports $120.21B = 6.83%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.55) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = N [0.3, 0.2, 0.55, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

regime_stability.unit: % per year (real, chain-linked); 10-year arithmetic mean (aggregate) / 10-year CAGR (per-capita)
regime_stability.derivation_method: Aggregate: Eurostat tec00115 direct read 2026-04-29, arithmetic mean over 11 obs 2014-2024. Per-capita: Eurostat sdg_08_10 chain-linked-volume 2020-EUR/inhabitant; CAGR from 18280→21060 over 10 years. Threshold flags per Bundle E spec: secular_stagnation if aggregate <1.5%; post_growth_empirical if per-capita <1.0%.
regime_stability.uncertainty_band: ±0.3pp on aggregate avg (Eurostat data revisions historically); ±0.5pp on per-capita CAGR (compounding effect of demographic series uncertainty); IE outlier — '24.6% in 2015' is leprechaun-economics artefact, statistically present but not a real-economy signal

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=4,224, 2035=5,083, Δ=+859; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=1,406, 2035=343, Δ=-1,063; [36] Water supply 2022=1,720, 2035=1,926, Δ=+206; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=2,430, 2035=2,773, Δ=+343; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=7,730, 2035=10,014, Δ=+2,284; [72] Research & Development 2022=3,030, 2035=4,624, Δ=+1,594; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=7,570, 2035=9,082, Δ=+1,512. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative: https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/files/skills_forecast_-_estonia_2025.pdf

value_b_carbon_displacement_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over carbon-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: CARBON-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 01 Agriculture, 02 Forestry, 03 Fishing, 05 Coal, 06 Oil and Gas, 07-09 Other mining, 19 Manufactured fuels (interpretive add to spec — pure refining/coking is structurally fossil); CARBON-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta < 0) = 10-12 Food/Drink/Tobacco, 16 Wood, 17 Paper, 18 Printing, 22 Rubber/plastic, 23 Non-metallic mineral, 24 Basic metals, 49 Land transport. Sub-sector breakdown: [01] Agriculture 2022=11,020, 2035=8,575, Δ=-2,445; [02] Forestry 2022=5,590, 2035=6,293, Δ=+703; [03] Fishing 2022=590, 2035=496, Δ=-94; [05] Coal 2022=0, 2035=0, Δ=+0; [06] Oil and Gas 2022=697, 2035=407, Δ=-290; [07-09] Other mining 2022=2,333, 2035=3,296, Δ=+963; [19] Manufactured fuels 2022=1,530, 2035=1,037, Δ=-493; [10-12] Food, Drink & Tobacco 2022=13,980, 2035=13,947, Δ=-33; [18] Printing 2022=2,840, 2035=2,558, Δ=-282; [22] Rubber and plastic products 2022=5,330, 2035=4,772, Δ=-558. Land transport [49] is the only transport sub-sector counted (water/air excluded — combustion-vehicle phase-out is the load-bearing carbon-displacement mechanism). Forestry/fishing show small positive deltas in many countries but retained per locked spec mapping (agriculture-cluster). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario with European Green Deal assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_b_carbon_displacement_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (45% for EL), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.45) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).

Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $7.46B + RU $2.64B / total imports $88.61B = 11.41%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.5) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.

Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = S [0.85, 0.85, 0.65, 0.9, 0.85, 0.65].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.note: 2023 Thessaly/'breadbasket' submerging — flood + ag H-confidence; chronic Med wildfire + drought

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (73% for FI), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.85) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

(relative-gains thinking, Zeitenwende), 2025 'Multipolarization', 2026 'Under Destruction' (wrecking-ball politics, Pax Americana under destruction). lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=30,106, 2035=32,915, Δ=+2,809; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=7,614, 2035=5,114, Δ=-2,500; [36] Water supply 2022=15,560, 2035=14,768, Δ=-792; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=29,330, 2035=21,896, Δ=-7,434; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=70,450, 2035=76,906, Δ=+6,456; [72] Research & Development 2022=33,820, 2035=60,531, Δ=+26,711. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (70% for HU), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.55) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

(relative-gains thinking, Zeitenwende), 2025 'Multipolarization', 2026 'Under Destruction' (wrecking-ball politics, Pax Americana under destruction). Per-country sentence selection: top-scored sentence (50-600 chars, contains country name, ranked by strategic-keyword density) from each available MSC report. lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $9.94B + RU $6.20B / total imports $150.65B = 10.72%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.55) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = CE [0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.note: Pannonian basin drought + heat hotspot — drought/heat regional-evidence M-confidence

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

regime_stability.unit: % per year (real, chain-linked 2023-ref); 10-year arithmetic mean (aggregate YoY) / 10-year CAGR (per-capita)
regime_stability.derivation_method: Modified GNI* substituted for headline GDP per Phil adjudication 2026-04-29 — eliminates 2015 corporate-domicile artefact (Apple/Google IP relocations drove +24.6% GDP). Aggregate: CSO PxStat NA002 'Modified Gross National Income at Constant Market Prices' (chain-linked, ref 2023), annual €M 2013-2024 → YoY series 2014-2024 → arithmetic mean over 11 obs. Per-capita: modGNI* €M divided by Eurostat tps00001 Jan-1 population; CAGR 45470→57061 over 10 years. Threshold flags per Bundle E spec: secular_stagnation if aggregate <1.5%; post_growth_empirical if per-capita <1.0%; aggregate_distributional_split if aggregate >1.5% AND per-capita <0.5%.
regime_stability.uncertainty_band: ±0.4pp on aggregate avg (modGNI* still exhibits residual pharma-export volatility — 2021 +13.76% is a real but lumpy post-COVID surge); ±0.5pp on per-capita CAGR (population revisions historically). Modified GNI* is the CSO's official correction for the leprechaun-economics distortion (IP migration, contract manufacturing); some Irish economists (Honohan, Coffey) argue further pharma-export smoothing would lower the read by another ~0.5-1pp.
regime_stability.note: Modified GNI* substituted for headline GDP per Phil adjudication 2026-04-29 — eliminates 2015 corporate-domicile artefact. Confidence demoted from H→M because (i) chain-linking-reference revision (2023-ref series, planned major revision per CSO) introduces methodological uncertainty, (ii) modified GNI* still includes pharma-sector volatility some analysts argue should be smoothed further. Both regime flags remain false at corrected reading; IE is a high-growth small open economy even after artefact correction.

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $11.55B + RU $0.08B / total imports $150.61B = 7.72%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.35) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = W [0.4, 0.45, 0.65, 0.45, 0.45, 0.6].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = N [0.3, 0.2, 0.55, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

regime_stability.unit: % per year (real, chain-linked); 10-year arithmetic mean (aggregate) / 10-year CAGR (per-capita)
regime_stability.derivation_method: Aggregate: Eurostat tec00115 direct read 2026-04-29, arithmetic mean over 11 obs 2014-2024. Threshold flags per Bundle E spec: secular_stagnation if aggregate <1.5%; post_growth_empirical if per-capita <1.0%.
regime_stability.uncertainty_band: ±0.3pp on aggregate avg (Eurostat data revisions historically); ±0.5pp on per-capita CAGR (compounding effect of demographic series uncertainty); IE outlier — '24.6% in 2015' is leprechaun-economics artefact, statistically present but not a real-economy signal

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=5,338, 2035=7,800, Δ=+2,462; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=4,862, 2035=5,275, Δ=+413; [36] Water supply 2022=1,643, 2035=1,642, Δ=-1; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=5,187, 2035=5,198, Δ=+11; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=9,500, 2035=9,057, Δ=-443; [72] Research & Development 2022=632, 2035=826, Δ=+194; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=3,935, 2035=4,662, Δ=+727. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative: https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/files/skills_forecast_-_latvia_2025.pdf

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (200% for LV), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.4) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens4_geopolitical_narrative.value: MSC 2026: "The result is a Europe moving at multiple speeds and scales on defense spending and Ukraine support – with a clear divide between fiscally solid high spenders in the northeast and fiscally strained lower spenders in the southwest – raising the risk of frictions over intra-European burden-sharing (Figure 2.4)." [Latvia named in Figure 2.4 'Fiscal and defense spending profiles of European NATO members, 2025']
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.derivation_method: Bundle G re-pass with country-name-only matching (relaxed from Bundle E session 2 keyword-score threshold). Direct read of MSR 2024/2025/2026 full PDFs via pdftotext -layout (Phil-supplied). Sentences extracted around named-mention sites; verbatim — no paraphrase.
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.uncertainty_band: verbatim citation; no estimation

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $0.94B + RU $0.66B / total imports $24.55B = 6.49%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.4) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = N [0.3, 0.2, 0.55, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=130,001, 2035=182,567, Δ=+52,566; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=64,599, 2035=59,320, Δ=-5,279; [36] Water supply 2022=60,863, 2035=59,887, Δ=-976; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=121,937, 2035=120,329, Δ=-1,608; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=168,251, 2035=283,290, Δ=+115,039; [72] Research & Development 2022=38,579, 2035=55,227, Δ=+16,648. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative: https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/files/skills_forecast_-_poland_2025.pdf
