lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (159% for PL), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.7) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens4_geopolitical_narrative.value: MSC 2026: "In September alone, around 20 Russian drones intruded into Polish airspace while three Russian MiG-31 fighter jets violated Estonian airspace for 12 minutes – prompting both governments to invoke NATO consultations under Article 4 of the North Atlantic Treaty." | MSC 2025: "“A safe Ukraine means Compounding the crisis, the new US administration has signaled a potential a safer Poland, Sweden, reduction in security assistance to the continent, forcing Europe to assume a Norway, Europe, and greater share of the burden of deterring Russia and supporting Ukraine."

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $51.52B + RU $2.67B / total imports $371.40B = 14.59%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.75) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = CE [0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

lens5d_munichre_losses.unit: USD billion (overall + insured losses per named event)
lens5d_munichre_losses.derivation_method: Direct read of Munich Re NatCAT-Stats 2025 + 2024 full-year factsheet PDFs (downloaded by Phil 2026-04-29, extracted via pdftotext -layout). Events tagged with multiple countries report joint figures with no per-country split. Drought/heatwave excluded by factsheet methodology rule.

europe_aggregate_2025.note: From 'Loss overview 2025 per continent' table; vs 10-yr avg ~$35B/$12B

europe_aggregate_2024.note: From 'Losses overview per continent in 2024' table — Europe column

lens5d_munichre_losses.data_gap_reason: Country not named in Munich Re 2024 or 2025 factsheet top-3 Europe ranking. Either (a) no event large enough to make top-3, (b) below USD-bn reporting threshold, or (c) impacted only as part of joint-country event that didn't reach top-3.

regime_stability.unit: % per year (real, chain-linked); 10-year arithmetic mean (aggregate) / 10-year CAGR (per-capita)
regime_stability.derivation_method: Aggregate: Eurostat tec00115 direct read 2026-04-29, arithmetic mean over 11 obs 2014-2024. Per-capita: Eurostat sdg_08_10 chain-linked-volume 2020-EUR/inhabitant; CAGR from 18560→22370 over 10 years. Threshold flags per Bundle E spec: secular_stagnation if aggregate <1.5%; post_growth_empirical if per-capita <1.0%.
regime_stability.uncertainty_band: ±0.3pp on aggregate avg (Eurostat data revisions historically); ±0.5pp on per-capita CAGR (compounding effect of demographic series uncertainty); IE outlier — '24.6% in 2015' is leprechaun-economics artefact, statistically present but not a real-economy signal

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (143% for RO), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.5) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens4_geopolitical_narrative.value: MSC 2026: "The US Global Force Posture Review remains pending, and only modest troop reductions have taken place in Romania – leaving European Allies relieved yet uncertain about the ultimate implications of Washington’s shifting priorities for their security."
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.derivation_method: Direct read of MSC PDFs (Phil-supplied 2026-04-29). MSC frames: 2024 'Lose-Lose?' (relative-gains thinking, Zeitenwende), 2025 'Multipolarization', 2026 'Under Destruction' (wrecking-ball politics, Pax Americana under destruction). Per-country sentence selection: top-scored sentence (50-600 chars, contains country name, ranked by strategic-keyword density) from each available MSC report. Reported in chronological order, most-recent first. Verbatim text in quotes.
lens4_geopolitical_narrative.uncertainty_band: Verbatim citation; uncertainty is in selection (which sentence best represents country framing). Sentence-level selection may miss broader context across the chapter; full-chapter read would refine.

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $7.31B + RU $0.35B / total imports $131.96B = 5.80%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.55) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = N [0.3, 0.2, 0.55, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.note: 2018 boreal wildfire season (~25,000 ha) — wildfire baseline raised within N-region

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=11,277, 2035=16,967, Δ=+5,690; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=6,083, 2035=6,030, Δ=-53; [36] Water supply 2022=10,300, 2035=11,536, Δ=+1,236; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=16,000, 2035=15,182, Δ=-818; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=34,900, 2035=43,635, Δ=+8,735; [72] Research & Development 2022=9,170, 2035=12,634, Δ=+3,464; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=38,050, 2035=48,609, Δ=+10,559. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (80% for SK), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.5) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $8.62B + RU $4.95B / total imports $115.36B = 11.76%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.5 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.65) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex

lens5c_klinger_coordination.derivation_method: Coordination-share is occupation-level (ISCO-3-digit), not country-level. v3 ESCO-derived: 125/130 ISCO-3 codes derived from real ESCO essential-skills tagging via transitive closure on ESCO skill hierarchy. 5 retain default-fallback. Same coefficients applied across all 36 countries. See layer-6-klinger-isco-coordination-share.json.
lens5c_klinger_coordination.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on derived; ±0.15 on default-fallback. Per-ISCO uncertainty in separate file.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = CE [0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).

lens5d_adaptation_budget.unit: EUR billion (totals); % share; EUR per capita (per-capita normalisations)
lens5d_adaptation_budget.derivation_method: Per-Member-State aggregates extracted from the Commission's RRF Sectoral Database (version 2026-01-23, supplied by Phil from the EU Research-on-the-RRF page). Computation: for each sub-measure row with Cost>0 (parent measures have Cost=0 to avoid double-counting), (i) total = sum of Cost; (ii) climate-tagged = sum of Cost × Climate Tag (coefficient 0-1 per Commission methodology); (iii) REPowerEU = sum of Cost where REPowerEU flag = Yes; (iv) adaptation-specific = sum of Cost × (Climate Tag or 1.0) for rows whose Green Objective Intervention field starts with 035 (floods), 036 (fires), 037 (storms/drought/other), 022 (research on resilience+adaptation), 027 (enterprise resilience services); plus 0.5 × water-partial-credit (field 040 — water resource conservation includes specific adaptation but also general supply, so partial credit applied). Per-capita normalised by Eurostat tps00001 2024 population.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.uncertainty_band: ±2% on totals (Commission's own publication; rounding within sectoral database). Adaptation-specific has higher uncertainty (±15%) — depends on the half-credit rule for water (field 040). If water-040 fully counted, adaptation share rises by ~30-50% in MS where water investments are significant (ES, IT, EL); if zero-credit, falls correspondingly. The 0.5 mid-point is methodologically defensible but defensible alternative weights exist.
lens5d_adaptation_budget.source: https://commission.europa.eu/strategy-and-policy/recovery-plan-europe (Research on the RRF: Sectoral data — RRF Sectoral Data_23.01.2026.xlsx, supplied by Phil 2026-04-29)

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=1,242, 2035=1,319, Δ=+77; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=458, 2035=525, Δ=+67; [36] Water supply 2022=0, 2035=0, Δ=+0; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=1,100, 2035=1,220, Δ=+120; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=2,800, 2035=3,356, Δ=+556; [72] Research & Development 2022=1,300, 2035=1,646, Δ=+346. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.

value_b_carbon_displacement_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=28,264, 2035=33,433, Δ=+5,169; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=1,446, 2035=1,447, Δ=+1; [36] Water supply 2022=1,969, 2035=2,066, Δ=+97; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=18,121, 2035=20,909, Δ=+2,788; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=137,590, 2035=150,796, Δ=+13,206; [72] Research & Development 2022=34,090, 2035=61,292, Δ=+27,202. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative PDF not part of standard country-report set for this jurisdiction

value_b_carbon_displacement_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over carbon-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: CARBON-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 01 Agriculture, 02 Forestry, 03 Fishing, 05 Coal, 06 Oil and Gas, 07-09 Other mining, 19 Manufactured fuels (interpretive add to spec — pure refining/coking is structurally fossil); CARBON-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta < 0) = 10-12 Food/Drink/Tobacco, 16 Wood, 17 Paper, 18 Printing, 22 Rubber/plastic, 23 Non-metallic mineral, 24 Basic metals, 49 Land transport. Sub-sector breakdown: [01] Agriculture 2022=112,139, 2035=112,970, Δ=+831; [02] Forestry 2022=7,588, 2035=7,217, Δ=-371; [03] Fishing 2022=723, 2035=687, Δ=-36; [05] Coal 2022=0, 2035=0, Δ=+0; [06] Oil and Gas 2022=0, 2035=0, Δ=+0; [07-09] Other mining 2022=4,650, 2035=4,991, Δ=+341; [19] Manufactured fuels 2022=584, 2035=523, Δ=-61; [10-12] Food, Drink & Tobacco 2022=86,230, 2035=79,513, Δ=-6,717; [17] Paper and paper products 2022=9,044, 2035=5,184, Δ=-3,860; [18] Printing 2022=19,546, 2035=14,501, Δ=-5,045; [24] Basic metals 2022=13,128, 2035=8,394, Δ=-4,734. Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario with European Green Deal assumptions. lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (26% for CH), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.6) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [CH BAZG Aussenhandel 2023: CN CHF17.8B + RU CHF0.34B / total CHF195B = 9.30%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.45 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.5) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.source: https://comtradeapi.un.org/public/v1/preview/C/A/HS (preview tier); supplementary: IISS Military Balance 2025 strategic-materials extracts; EU CRMA Reg. (EU) 2024/1252 strategic raw materials annex
lens5a_trade_decoupling.note: Component (a) computed from national-statistics fallback because Comtrade preview returned 0 records for this reporter (CH).

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = W [0.4, 0.45, 0.65, 0.45, 0.45, 0.6].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). Direction-of-travel signals from EUCRA Figure ES.1 are robust; absolute calibration on 0-1 scale is methodological (EUCRA does not publish per-country numerical scores).
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.note: Not EU-EEA member; W-region baseline with Alpine adjustment (drought/infrastructure raised for glacier loss + mountain hazards). Confidence L.

lens5d_eea_vulnerability.derivation_method: EUCRA 2024 (EEA Report 01/2024) aggregates climate risks by 4 land macro-regions (Northern/Western/Central-Eastern/Southern Europe) + outermost regions, not by country. Country-level scores derived by: (1) assigning country to its EUCRA macro-region, (2) setting region baseline per 6 sub-dimensions [wildfire/drought/flood/heat-outdoor/agricultural/infrastructure] from EUCRA Figure ES.1 direction-of-travel + Figure ES.4 urgency clusters, (3) overriding with EUCRA-named country events (Germany+Belgium 2021 €44B floods, Slovenia 2023 16%-GDP floods, Greece 2023 breadbasket flooding, Iberia 2022-2024 megadrought, Portugal 2017+2022 wildfires, UK 2022 40°C record, Po 2022 drought) and (4) supplementary domain evidence (water scarcity per capita for CY/MT, EFFIS wildfire records for S Europe, Pannonian drought for HU, Alpine glacier-loss for CH/AT). Composite = arithmetic mean of 6 sub-dimensions. Region baseline = CE [0.5, 0.6, 0.65, 0.55, 0.55, 0.55].
lens5d_eea_vulnerability.uncertainty_band: ±0.10 on most cells; ±0.15 for CH/LI/TR (alpine/non-member proxy) and BA/MK/RS (CE proxy outside EUCRA scope). value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=6,816, 2035=7,739, Δ=+923; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=328, 2035=577, Δ=+249; [36] Water supply 2022=5,271, 2035=6,865, Δ=+1,594; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=3,982, 2035=5,655, Δ=+1,673; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=5,440, 2035=8,131, Δ=+2,691; [72] Research & Development 2022=463, 2035=763, Δ=+300; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=2,043, 2035=3,266, Δ=+1,223. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative PDF not part of standard country-report set for this jurisdiction

value_b_carbon_displacement_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Land transport [49] is the only transport sub-sector counted (water/air excluded — combustion-vehicle phase-out is the load-bearing carbon-displacement mechanism). regime_stability.unit: % per year (real, chain-linked); 10-year arithmetic mean (aggregate) / 10-year CAGR (per-capita)
regime_stability.derivation_method: Aggregate: Eurostat tec00115 direct read 2026-04-29, arithmetic mean over 11 obs 2014-2024. Per-capita: Eurostat sdg_08_10 chain-linked-volume 2020-EUR/inhabitant; CAGR from 6500→9220 over 10 years. Threshold flags per Bundle E spec: secular_stagnation if aggregate <1.5%; post_growth_empirical if per-capita <1.0%.
regime_stability.uncertainty_band: ±0.3pp on aggregate avg (Eurostat data revisions historically); ±0.5pp on per-capita CAGR (compounding effect of demographic series uncertainty); IE outlier — '24.6% in 2015' is leprechaun-economics artefact, statistically present but not a real-economy signal

value_a_green_jobs_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over green-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: GREEN-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 35.1 Electricity, 35.2-25.3 Gas/steam/AC, 36 Water supply, 37-39 Sewerage and waste, 71 Architectural & engineering, 72 R&D; GREEN-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta > 0) = 27 Electrical equipment. Sub-sector breakdown: [35.1] Electricity 2022=129,407, 2035=146,212, Δ=+16,805; [35.2-25.3] Gas, steam & air conditioning 2022=12,970, 2035=13,309, Δ=+339; [36] Water supply 2022=32,239, 2035=72,511, Δ=+40,272; [37-39] Sewerage and waste 2022=161,537, 2035=136,599, Δ=-24,938; [71] Architectural & engineering 2022=181,270, 2035=174,682, Δ=-6,588; [72] Research & Development 2022=16,636, 2035=16,633, Δ=-3; [27] Electrical equipment 2022=238,863, 2035=239,815, Δ=+952. Construction [41-43] excluded — renovation/insulation/renewable share not separable in NACE-2d data (acknowledged green undercount). R&D and Architectural & engineering attributed in full per locked spec; true climate-attributable share within these sectors is lower (no green-task coding available without ESCO/O*NET join). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario incorporating European Green Deal investment + power-sector + carbon-pricing assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.uncertainty_band: ±10-15% on Cedefop 2035-horizon projections (validation note in dataset documentation: AMECO macro projection uncertainty over 13-year forecast; Eurostat data-revision risk on 2022 baseline; sub-sector mix shifts under non-linear policy paths). Mapping-attribution uncertainty additionally widens band: R&D + Architectural & engineering counted in full but only a share is climate-coupled; would tighten by ~30-50% if green-task coding (ESCO/O*NET join) were applied. Combined effective band ±20% per Bundle F spec.
value_a_green_jobs_2035.source: Cedefop Skills Forecast 2025 Employment_sector_detail.xlsx (local data registry); country narrative PDF not part of standard country-report set for this jurisdiction

value_b_carbon_displacement_2035.derivation_method: Cedefop 2025 Skills Forecast Employment_sector_detail dataset (66 NACE 2-digit sub-sectors, annual 2010-2035, absolute headcount). Sum of 2022→2035 employment delta over carbon-relevant sub-sectors per Bundle F locked mapping: CARBON-UNCONDITIONAL (counted always) = 01 Agriculture, 02 Forestry, 03 Fishing, 05 Coal, 06 Oil and Gas, 07-09 Other mining, 19 Manufactured fuels (interpretive add to spec — pure refining/coking is structurally fossil); CARBON-CONDITIONAL (counted only if delta < 0) = 10-12 Food/Drink/Tobacco, 16 Wood, 17 Paper, 18 Printing, 22 Rubber/plastic, 23 Non-metallic mineral, 24 Basic metals, 49 Land transport. Sub-sector breakdown: [01] Agriculture 2022=5,325,667, 2035=3,874,840, Δ=-1,450,827; [02] Forestry 2022=43,023, 2035=72,165, Δ=+29,142; [03] Fishing 2022=29,485, 2035=47,972, Δ=+18,487; [05] Coal 2022=48,874, 2035=49,887, Δ=+1,013; [06] Oil and Gas 2022=2,868, 2035=3,025, Δ=+157; [07-09] Other mining 2022=101,190, 2035=208,134, Δ=+106,944; [19] Manufactured fuels 2022=14,456, 2035=14,076, Δ=-380; [16] Wood and wood products 2022=110,827, 2035=99,603, Δ=-11,224; [24] Basic metals 2022=246,780, 2035=245,785, Δ=-995. Land transport [49] is the only transport sub-sector counted (water/air excluded — combustion-vehicle phase-out is the load-bearing carbon-displacement mechanism). Forestry/fishing show small positive deltas in many countries but retained per locked spec mapping (agriculture-cluster). Source: Cedefop elaborations on Eurostat (LFS, National Accounts, EUROPOP) and DG-ECFIN AMECO projections, baseline scenario with European Green Deal assumptions. Local file: european-ai-exposure-map/data/cedefop/skills-forecast-2025/Employment_sector_detail.xlsx.

lens4_geopolitical.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in %; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens4_geopolitical.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) SIPRI Fact Sheet April 2025 Table 1 — military expenditure 2015-24 real % change (110% for TR), normalised /200 with cap 1; (b) reshoring band (0.45) reflects EU CRMA Strategic Projects host status (Commission March 2024 first list, 47 projects/13 MS) + critical-mineral deposit endowment; (c) migration-flow volatility = coefficient of variation of asylum applications 2022-2024 from Eurostat migr_asyappctza, normalised /0.5 cap. Weighting choice: defence-labour-demand-growth weighted 0.5 (largest single labour-reallocation driver in scope per IISS Military Balance 2025 ramp-up section); reshoring weighted 0.2 (per-MS data sparse; aggregate-EU CRMA structure); migration 0.3 (volatility material to labour-supply variability).
lens4_geopolitical.uncertainty_band: Component a: ±5pp on SIPRI top-40; ±20pp on supplementary IISS/NATO estimates (EE/LV/LT/BG/HR/SK/HU/PT/SI/CY/AT/IE/MT/LU). Component b: ±0.10 (qualitative band; per-MS CRMA allocation not formally published as %s). Component c: CoV stable at 3-year window but sensitive to 2025 partial-year exclusion.
lens4_geopolitical.source: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database / Fact Sheet April 2025 (https://www.sipri.org/sites/default/files/2025-04/2504_fs_milex_2024.pdf); Eurostat migr_asyappctza; EU Commission CRMA Strategic Projects list (March 2024)

lens5a_trade_decoupling.unit: Composite 0-1; component a in % of total imports; b/c on 0-1 normalised scale
lens5a_trade_decoupling.derivation_method: Composite = a*0.5 + b*0.2 + c*0.3, where: (a) imports-from-(CN+RU) share / total imports normalised by 0.20 cap [UN Comtrade preview 2023: imports from CN $45.05B + RU $45.60B / total imports $361.97B = 25.04%]; (b) EU dual-use export-share proxy (uniform 0.4 for EU; separate regime values for UK/EFTA/candidates per Commission 2024 Annual Report on Export Controls — EU-aggregate ~6% of total goods exports are dual-use); (c) strategic-materials China-dependency band (0.65) reflecting industrial-concentration in defence (IISS Military Balance 2025: nitrocellulose + electronics + armour steel China-supply named) + EU CRMA strategic raw materials list (REE/permanent magnets/battery materials) per-MS exposure.
lens5a_trade_decoupling.uncertainty_band: ±0.05 on composite for COMTRADE-derived (a); ±0.10 for PUBLISHED-fallback (a). Component b is EU-aggregate proxy — true per-MS dual-use export shares published only at EU level. Component c is qualitative band (0.05 step granularity) — calibrated against IISS attestation + CRMA per-MS REE/critical-raw-materials exposure list; could be tightened with explicit per-MS export-control filings.
